questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{3} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(\sqrt{3})^{2}+{3}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =3+9 \\ {R}^{2} & =12 \\ R & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+{60}^{∘})
$$

questions.problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Express $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ in the form $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with $ϕ\in (0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ Use the **exact value** for $R,$ and round $ϕ$ to **three decimal places**.

$2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈$
{{field-1}}
$\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\,+$
{{field-2}}$)$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+7\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & =(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=7\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{7}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{7}{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{7}{2}) \\ ϕ & ≈1.292\,\text{rad},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡(ϕ)+{R}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡(ϕ) & ={7}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡(ϕ)+{cos}^{2}⁡(ϕ)) & =49+4 \\ {R}^{2} & =53 \\ R & =\sqrt{53}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+7\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)≈\sqrt{53}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+1.292)
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Cosine
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{3}{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={3}^{2}+{3}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =9+9 \\ {R}^{2} & =18 \\ R & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=3\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+{45}^{∘})
$$
